brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: vocabulary.get
objective.description: Return the filtered global semantic vocabulary, either as JSON or as the LLM-readable text map.

#root.role: Run a root-only vocabulary document read and return either the filtered global vocabulary JSON or its LLM-readable four-axis path map.

file._comment: Selects which root projection vocabulary artifact to read. json reads projection/vocabulary.json. llm reads projection/vocabulary.llm.txt.

vocabulary._comment: Present when params.file is absent or equals json.

effects.vocabulary_overlay: The selected root vocabulary artifact is read-only.

transformation_contract.morphing: A root vocabulary get request becomes either the complete vocabulary JSON document stored in projection/vocabulary.json or the LLM-readable text map stored in projection/vocabulary.llm.txt.
invariants: vocabulary.get reads the selected materialized vocabulary artifact without mutating projection state.
Both artifacts expose only the brique, objective, functional, and subjective semantic axes.
The json file applies the same generic semantic-path and compact-value policy as the SQLite vocabulary projection.
The llm file is a text-only hierarchical path map over the four axes and does not include vocabulary values.
success: On success with file=json, vocabulary.get returns payload.file='json' and payload.vocabulary as the complete vocabulary JSON object.
On success with file=llm, vocabulary.get returns payload.file='llm' and payload.content as the complete LLM-readable vocabulary text.
failure: The capacity is refused outside the root context.
The capacity fails when params.file is not one of json|llm.
The capacity fails when the selected vocabulary artifact is unavailable or cannot be decoded/read.
notes: vocabulary.get returns all four axes in one document; prefer vocabulary.query when one complete semantic axis is sufficient.
vocabulary.query remains JSON projection-only and is not affected by params.file.

The vocabulary is intentionally smaller than the meaning index: identity, revision, locator, long prose, URL, filesystem-path, UUID, and long-hash data are omitted. In particular, any path segment named name is excluded. Those fields remain indexed and queryable through meaning.query.

This is a projection snapshot, not a live mirror of the filesystem: nothing in the engine calls meaning.rebuild or meaning.update automatically when descriptors are created, edited, or deleted (edit.create, edit.patch_meaning, matter.write, etc. never touch the projection). A vocabulary that looks sparse relative to the real number of contexts/capacities/matters on disk almost always means the projection predates most of that content, not that the content is absent. Before relying on this vocabulary to navigate an unfamiliar or long-lived world, call meaning.rebuild (mode=vocabulary-only is enough for this capacity) if you have no recent evidence the projection is current — do not assume a rebuild done earlier in an unrelated session still covers what exists now.
